Article Title: More teachers, better access, fewer pupils: India’s government school paradox
Article Text:
Gujarat Government school

From buffaloes and buckets to what the national numbers say

Nearly 1 lakh fewer govt schools, but access improves on paper

Nearly 1 lakh less government school in 10 years

Govt schools are losing pupils even as the system improves

Drop-outs decreasing

Basic access gap remains

Schools are back in focus. In larger policy discussions and political debates. The Opposition, emboldened by its NEET protest victory, is looking to up the ante by exposing ramshackle school infrastructure in different states, starting with Rajasthan. TOI ground reports, too, have found gross inadequacies in government schools across different parts of the state. Particularly jarring is the fact that in Kota , widely called the coaching capital of India, many government schools are in a dilapidated state. wider ground report by TOI reporters across the country found that Rajasthan was hardly an outlier. In Bihar, nearly 200 children from four classes were sharing a single room at one school while cattle occupied two others. In Uttarakhand, leaking roofs meant buckets and umbrellas had become classroom fixtures. In Madhya Pradesh, TOI found schools struggling with teacher shortages and unsafe buildings. Keralam was a prominent exception to this broader picture.However, the fact remains that in a country of 1.4 billion people, structural gaps are perhaps expected, if certainly not desired. A good metric of how much the school system has improved over the years is to look at the data furnished by the central government and its allied agencies.The pan-India numbers make for interesting reading. Rajasthan had 7,200 single-teacher schools in 2025-26, while only 36.4% of schools reported ramps with handrails and 26.3% had toilets tailored for Children with Special Needs (CwSN).The country has nearly a lakh fewer government schools than it did a decade ago, and those schools are losing pupils. It also has more teachers, far fewer children in single-teacher schools, more teenagers reaching higher secondary and internet access in about two-thirds of schools. Fewer than half of schools, however, report a toilet designed for children with special needs. Yet despite improvements in many metrics, government-school enrolment is falling.Most of what is known about India's schools comes from UDISE+, the Unified District Information System for Education Plus. It is an annual, census-like administrative database covering schools across management types. Schools report on their pupils, teachers and infrastructure, from enrolment and staffing to toilets, electricity, ramps, computers and internet access, and they are incorporated into the Union education ministry's national school statistics.The system grew out of UDISE, created in 2012-13 by merging separate elementary and secondary databases. UDISE+ became its online successor from 2018-19. The government uses it to locate infrastructure gaps, and states draw on it when seeking support for classrooms, toilets, drinking water, electricity, libraries and digital facilities under schemes such as Samagra Shiksha.A school can figure in the database as open and equipped with a particular facility, but reality can be very different. TOI's visits across states repeatedly brought out that distinction.India had 11,04,796 government schools in 2015-16. Ten years later, UDISE+ records 10,05,245, a difference of 99,551 schools or 9%. The rider is that a school leaving the UDISE count can reflect closure, merger, rationalisation, reclassification or other administrative change.The decline is stark in some states. Madhya Pradesh had 1,21,976 government schools in 2015-16; by 2025-26 the count was 91,199, a reduction of 30,777. Uttar Pradesh fell from 1,62,645 to 1,37,103, a reduction of 25,542. Together, the two states account for about 56.6% of the national net decline over the decade.There have also been changes in school mapping and verification, with UDISE+ replacing the older UDISE system from 2018-19. Questioned in Parliament, the Centre has said that decisions on opening, closing and rationalising schools lie largely with states and Union territories, while the Right to Education framework requires elementary schools to remain accessible within prescribed neighbourhood limits.Between 2018-19 and 2024-25, the Gross Access Ratio rose from 88.24% to 95.35% at the secondary level and from 65.05% to 94.97% at higher secondary. GAR measures the proportion of habitations or villages with a school available within the prescribed distance; it is not an enrolment ratio. So although there are fewer schools, the measured access ratio has improved. This is also part of the government's defence.Government-school enrolment fell from 12.75 crore in 2023-24 to 11.89 crore in 2025-26, nearly 85.9 lakh fewer pupils in just two years, a decline of 6.7%. Over the same period, enrolment in private unaided schools rose from 9.00 crore to 9.89 crore, an increase of about 88.3 lakh, or 9.8%. The thinning out is also visible over a decade with average enrolment per government school falling from about 132 pupils in 2014-15 to 120 in 2024-25, a decline of roughly 9%; the latest UDISE+ figures put it at about 118 in 2025-26.One figure from the government's own parliamentary reply captures the scale of it. In 2024-25, government institutions accounted for 68.9% of all schools in India but 49.2% of all enrolment.A movement this large might be expected to have triggered a substantial investigation. On July 29, 2026, the government was asked why government-school enrolment had fallen from about 12.8 crore to 11.9 crore while private enrolment rose from around 9 crore to 9.9 crore.The ministry confirmed the numbers but did not cite or summarise such an assessment in its reply. Instead, it listed the interventions being made to strengthen government education.NITI Aayog's 2026 UDISE+-based review says the broader decline in enrolment through 2024-25 is partly attributable to demographic shifts, particularly falling fertility and a smaller school-age population, alongside school consolidation and challenges in retaining pupils at higher levels.Ranabir Bhattacharyya, teacher-in-charge of the English-medium primary section of Chetla Boys' High School in Kolkata, points to some of the practical issues with UDISE+ and also offers context for the dwindling numbers. He says the data had many issues at one point, but the pipeline has increasingly been made more robust as the government seeks to bring all students onto the platform to roll out various developmental schemes aimed at schoolchildren.He alleges that there was earlier an incentive in certain quarters to inflate pupil numbers, but says tighter vigilance has reduced that tendency and the numbers now being reflected are closer to reality. Ranabir, however, flags other problems like the website can be difficult to use and often suffers technical glitches, while the absence of additional staff increases the workload of those responsible for keeping the data updated. As a result, underreporting can happen too, according to him.India had 96.96 lakh teachers in 2020-21 and 102.73 lakh in 2025-26, nearly 5.77 lakh additional teachers in five years. Single-teacher schools fell from 1,10,971 in 2023-24 to 1,00,843 in 2025-26, and the number of children enrolled in them dropped more steeply still, from 39.94 lakh to 29.12 lakh. Nearly 11 lakh fewer children are now in such schools.But the national improvement hides striking state differences. Andhra Pradesh alone has 16,357 single-teacher schools; Jharkhand has 9,827, Maharashtra 9,269, Karnataka 8,042 and Uttar Pradesh 7,874. Those five states together account for just over half of India's 1,00,843 single-teacher schools.And this is one area where the statistical picture intersects sharply with what TOI reporters saw. In Madhya Pradesh, TOI found 70 children and one teacher operating from a single dilapidated room at a school in Bhopal's Kolar, while students in Classes XI and XII at a PM SHRI school in Mandla had gone without teachers for newly introduced streams for a year.Uttarakhand has 2,655 single-teacher schools, about 11.8% of its entire school network, alongside its unusually high proportion of very small schools. The Centre acknowledges the problem. It has told Parliament that recruitment and postings are primarily state responsibilities; and that it repeatedly presses states on faster recruitment and redeployment while supporting them under Samagra Shiksha.Ranabir highlights another issue involving children of migrant labourers. He says that when a student shifts from one school to another, the subsequent UDISE+ entry does not always move smoothly as it requires manual intervention. West Bengal School Education Minister Dipak Barman, speaking to TOI, says many private schools in the state have not uploaded their student lists. Barman says the state is working to get the figures updated. It is hard to know whether similar anomalies exist elsewhere, but if they do, they could significantly undermine the purpose of what the central government is trying to achieve with the UDISE+ platform.The encouraging part is that reported dropout rates are falling. In many states, girl students are incentivised to continue school education. At the same time, higher-secondary Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) rose from 56.2% in 2023-24 to 61.7% in 2025-26, and the secondary dropout rate fell from 14.1% to 9.5% over the same period. Here too, the national number hides enormous variation. Keralam, for instance, reported secondary retention of 99.1% in 2025-26.For many from financially weaker sections, there is a significant opportunity cost to staying in school after Class X. The government has therefore deployed a range of measures to keep more students in the system. Parliamentary replies point to PM POSHAN, residential schools and hostels, KGBVs, transport assistance, free textbooks and uniforms, enrolment campaigns and vocational education, and more recently to Vidya Samiksha Kendras and APAAR IDs as tools for tracking students who drop out or move between schools.In step with the government's Digital India push, digital infrastructure has expanded rapidly. In 2020-21, 24.5% of schools reported internet access; by 2025-26, 67.4% did. Computer availability rose from 41.3% to 69.9%. The approved budget for ICT labs, smart classrooms and other digital initiatives rose from ₹381.1 crore in 2018-19 to ₹3,221.1 crore in 2025-26.NITI Aayog's 2026 UDISE+-based analysis of functional smart classrooms shows coverage rising from 14.9% of schools in 2021-22 to 30.6% in 2024-25. In other words, even after rapid expansion, nearly seven in ten schools still lacked one.The interstate divide is striking. Punjab reported functional smart classrooms in 80.1% of schools and Delhi in 75.7%; the corresponding figures were only 4.3% in Meghalaya, 5.7% in West Bengal, 14.9% in Bihar and 19.8% in Uttar Pradesh. Tamil Nadu offers the opposite story: its reported coverage went from virtually zero in 2021-22 to 60.8% in 2024-25.TOI's ground visits underline why infrastructure numbers need context. In Uttar Pradesh, schools visited by reporters had toilets and drinking water, but digital resources were missing; in Himachal Pradesh, strong coverage of basic facilities coexisted with substantially weaker smart-classroom and disability-access indicators.Regarding West Bengal's poor showing, Barman says many of the state's UDISE+ figures have not been properly updated and that the government is working to correct them, and is looking to start 2000 smart classrooms in the next one year. He says Bengal expects to be among the top 10 when the next calculation is made.India is now close to universal provision of toilet facilities in schools, at least on paper. UDISE+ reports girls'-toilet availability in 98.5% of girls' and co-educational schools in 2025-26. But availability and functionality are not the same.TOI's ground reporting provides a simple illustration of that distinction. Schools visited in Uttar Pradesh had separate toilets for boys and girls, but reporters found many of them unclean, with teachers blaming the absence of sanitation workers. This issue of not having adequate sanitation staff is something Ranabir also flagged repeatedly.The same NITI Aayog analysis, using 2024-25 data, puts national functional girls'-toilet coverage at 94%, up from 85.17% a decade earlier. Yet the state map remains uneven.In 2024-25, Bihar and Odisha were both at 98.1% functional girls'-toilet coverage and West Bengal at 99.6%, while Rajasthan stood at 87.3%. Meghalaya was at 68.7%, Arunachal Pradesh 73.7% and Manipur 74.5%.In 2020-21, 24.5% of schools reported internet access and 41.3% computers. About 48.3% reported ramps with handrails and 25.3% toilets for children with special needs. By 2025-26, internet availability had reached 67.4% and computers 69.9%. Ramps with handrails were at 58.2%, while CwSN-friendly toilets stood at only 40.1%.The state contrasts are revealing. Himachal Pradesh reports functional electricity in 99.1% of schools and computers in 87.2%, but internet reaches only 66.2% and CwSN-friendly toilets 34%. At the same time, 18.3% of its schools are single-teacher schools and almost half have 30 pupils or fewer.Keralam, the prominent exception in TOI's ground reporting, also stands apart on several UDISE measures. Computer availability is 99.5%, internet access 92.6%, and only 67 schools, about 0.4% of its network, are single-teacher schools. Secondary retention is 99.1%. The state is not without gaps, only around 51.7% of schools report CwSN-friendly toilets but the overall contrast with many other states is striking.The Accessibility Code was notified in 2024, and Samagra Shiksha and PM SHRI provide funds for facility upliftment. Ranabir says funds often come in a trickle or are regularly delayed. As a result, he says, many of these metrics do not improve as smoothly as desired. He also highlights that many rural schools have irregular electricity supply, and hence while internet and other digital facilities are present on paper, reality can be different.Taken together, most of these service and outcome indicators have moved positively. Yet government-school enrolment is falling. That may partly reflect an aspirational society where some parents are looking to private schools for stronger English-language exposure, soft skills, peer networks and perceived advantages in college and beyond. Anecdotally, one can also see the mushrooming of English-medium schools in suburbs and mofussils.But the national data do not by themselves establish why families make these choices. Some of the decline may also reflect cleaner data and ironically even lack of proper uploading of data as pointed out by the Bengal education minister.There is no one-size-fits-all solution for such a large country. The data show substantial progress on several fronts, yet the lived reality may be different in some places. For now, the government will need to tick the boxes on what should be absolutely non-negotiable in terms of core deliverables, including the lacunae exposed in those reports. Winning the larger battle for aspiration may be a challenge for another day, or another decade.
Article Summary: India has nearly a lakh fewer government schools than it did a decade ago. It also has more teachers, far fewer children in single-teacher schools, more teenagers reaching higher secondary and internet access in about two-thirds of schools. Fewer than half of schools report a toilet designed for children with special needs.

Article Title: PM Modi takes stock of flood situation in Varanasi as water crosses warning mark
Article Text:
The Prime Minister directed the district administration to work on a war footing to provide relief to those affected

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday spoke to Varanasi District Magistrate Satyendra Kumar and took stock of the flood situation in the city as the rising water level of the Ganga crossed the warning mark amid incessant rainfall.PM Modi, who is also the Member of Parliament from Varanasi, sought detailed information from the district magistrate about the river's water level and the arrangements being made at relief camps for people affected by the floods.The Prime Minister directed the district administration to work on a war footing to provide relief to those affected and ensure that all necessary facilities are made available immediately.He also instructed officials to make immediate arrangements wherever there is an additional requirement for relief material and expedite relief work for affected people.PM Modi further directed the administration to maintain constant vigilance over the flood situation and relief operations and ensure that immediate assistance reaches those affected.The Prime Minister's intervention came as the Ganga continued to rise in Varanasi.According to the Central Water Commission (CWC), the river's water level reached 70.54 metres at the Rajghat gauge site at 6 am on Thursday, crossing the warning level of 70.262 metres. The water level was rising at a rate of 2 cm per hour.The danger level at the site is 71.262 metres, while the highest flood level is 73.901 metres.The district administration has been closely monitoring areas affected by the rising waters of the Ganga and Varuna rivers. On Tuesday, District Magistrate Satyendra Kumar and Varanasi Police Commissioner Mohit Agrawal inspected several flood-affected areas after travelling by an NDRF boat from Namo Ghat.The officials visited Salarpur, Saraiya, Konia, Pul Kohna, Dhelvaria and Sarai Mohana to assess waterlogging and the situation of residents. They also interacted with affected people and assured them of all possible assistance.The district magistrate directed officials to remain on high alert and keep arrangements ready to shift residents to safer locations. He also ordered that boats and other resources remain available for relief and rescue operations.Relief camps at the Primary School in Salarpur and Vidya Vihar Inter College were also inspected. Officials were directed to ensure adequate food, drinking water, electricity, lighting, sanitation, healthcare and security, with special attention to children, women and elderly people.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi spoke to Varanasi District Magistrate Satyendra Kumar. He took stock of the flood situation in the city as the rising water level of the Ganga crossed the warning mark amid incessant rainfall. The Prime Minister directed the district administration to work on a war footing to provide relief to those affected.

Article Title: Tamil for Madras HC: CM Vijay to move resolution urging Centre's approval
Article Text:
Tamil Nadu increases milk procurement price by Rs 6, says CM Joseph Vijay

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay is set to move a resolution in the state assembly on Thursday urging the Centre to recognise Tamil as the principal language of the Madras high court , official sources said.The resolution will be moved by Vijay during the assembly session and is likely to be taken up for discussion. It will seek a formal framework to ensure that judgments, decrees and judicial orders of the high court are also made available in Tamil.The move is expected to highlight Tamil's status as a classical language. It will also point to the significant development of legal terminology in Tamil. The resolution is likely to cite technology-enabled translation facilities as another factor supporting the proposal.The state government will also refer to the existing legal provisions governing the use of regional languages in high court proceedings and judgments. Under the current framework, a state's official language can be used in addition to English, but this requires the Governor's authorisation and the prior consent of the President.The resolution is also expected to recall an earlier attempt by the Tamil Nadu assembly. On December 6, 2006, the House had passed a resolution seeking the use of Tamil in the Madras high court. The resolution was subsequently forwarded to the Union government.The latest proposal seeks to revive the demand and push for Tamil to be recognised as the principal language of the Madras high court.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay is set to move a resolution urging the Centre to recognise Tamil as the principal language of the Madras high court. The resolution will be moved by Vijay during the assembly session and is likely to be taken up for discussion. The move is expected to highlight Tamil's status as a classical language.

Article Title: ‘No record’: Podcaster’s claim reignites row over CJP founder’s BU degree; Dipke hits back with video
Article Text:
A controversy has resurfaced regarding Abhijeet Dipke's educational credentials from Boston University

Sonam Wangchuk on Dipke’s political ambitions





NEW DELHI: A fresh controversy has erupted over Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke’s educational credentials after podcaster Prakhar Gupta said one of his friends who studied at Boston University could not find a record of Dipke’s graduation there.The claim was made during an episode of The Prakhar Gupta Xperience podcast featuring climate activist Sonam Wangchuk.Gupta said one of his close friends had studied at Boston University and had been actively involved in supporting the CJP-led protest at Jantar Mantar.“One of my best friends went to Boston University. It is also Abhijeet’s college,” Gupta said during the podcast.He said his friend had participated in the protests and produced media content in support of the movement.Gupta claimed that about a month later, his friend began looking into Dipke’s educational credentials and allegedly found no record of him graduating from Boston University.“He has gone down the rabbit hole of checking up Abhijeet’s education credentials and found there is no record of him graduating from Boston University,” Gupta said.Dipke, however, responded to the claim on X, appearing to mock the suggestion that his graduation could not be verified.“Not my fault that his friends were not invited at BU COM Grad events,” Dipke wrote, while sharing a video appearing to show him at an event associated with Boston University’s College of Communication graduate community.The video was a screen recording of a story posted by an Instagram account identified as “BU COM Grad, Student Council”.The latest allegation comes despite Boston University itself having published material identifying Dipke as a graduate.In a June 2026 article, Boston University’s College of Communication described Dipke as a “COM grad” and said he had completed his master’s in public relations from the university the previous year.The university article also carried an interview with Dipke in which he discussed how his studies at BU influenced the communication strategy behind the CJP campaign.Dipke has previously maintained that he studied at Boston University and earned a master’s degree in public relations. He has also said his education was financed through a Boston University scholarship and an education loan.Amid the controversy, Dipke had earlier said he was willing to produce his degree and other documents to establish his educational credentials.The dispute has now resurfaced as Dipke and the CJP leadership face increasing scrutiny over their backgrounds and political ambitions following the movement’s prolonged protests over examination-related issues.The same podcast also featured Wangchuk discussing Dipke and other CJP organisers, including their possible political ambitions.Wangchuk said he believed Dipke and his fellow organisers appeared to have political aspirations, although they had not explicitly told him about any such plans. He said there was nothing inherently wrong with political ambitions as long as the CJP remained a non-party platform.“Political ambition is very normal,” Wangchuk said, adding that he did not care about the organisers’ past political connections and had no problem with their present or future political aspirations.Wangchuk also said the organisers were not necessarily acting entirely selflessly and described them as “well meaning”, “quite skilled” and “above average”. He cautioned that their political aspirations should not turn the CJP platform itself into a vehicle for any political party.He said the organisers could eventually join an existing political party or form one of their own, but should preserve CJP as a “neutral, apolitical pressure group”.The comments came days before the Supreme Court quashed 127 FIRs filed against student protesters in five states in connection with the CJP agitation.Following assurances given before the court, CJP called off its proposed September 5 march from India Gate to Delhi Police headquarters.
Article Summary: A fresh controversy has erupted over Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke's educational credentials. Podcaster Prakhar Gupta said one of his friends who studied at Boston University could not find a record of Dipke’s graduation there. The claim was made during an episode of The PrakHar Gupta Xperience podcast featuring climate activist Sonam Wangchuk.

Article Title: Nitin Gadkari urges all state governments to allow bike taxis; announces plan for negative points for traffic rule violations
Article Text:
File photo: Union minister Nitin Gadkari

NEW DELHI: Union road transport minister Nitin Gadkari Wednesday urged all state govts to allow bike taxis, saying it could give employment to eight crore people.During the launch of a pilot programme — “Suraksha” — for on-the-spot free medical diagnosis and counselling for 10 lakh drivers, construction and high-risk workers involved in building highways and mines, he also said his ministry will amend Motor Vehicles Act to introduce a negative point system for drivers for traffic violations, which will result in suspension and cancellation of driving licence.The initiative will be implemented on 150-km covering Nagpur–Kamptee areas of NH-44 and mining belt in Chandrapur in Maharashtra, with a target of 10,000 people.Speaking about the programme, Gadkari sought better medical tests and healthcare for drivers and construction workers, saying that “health of our drivers is key for road safety and there is a dire need to focus on their eyecare and other health issues they face due to the nature of their work.”On the need to allow private two-wheelers, such as scooters and motorcycles, owners to allow transporting passengers, he said this will create employment opportunities in rural areas. “We have allowed this. But some states are not allowing this. Transport is a state subject. I will urge them to do so as this will give a source of livelihood to many,” Gadkari said.Highlighting the high number of deaths and violations of traffic and transport rules by drivers, the minister said that they have finalised the proposed legislation to penalise the “habitual offenders”. He said, “There will be negative points for each violation and accumulation of a certain point will result in suspension and even cancellation of licences. We hope this will instil responsible driving behaviour,” he said.
Article Summary: Union road transport minister Nitin Gadkari Wednesday urged all state govts to allow bike taxis. He also said his ministry will introduce a negative point system for drivers for traffic violations, which will result in suspension and cancellation of driving licence.

Article Title: SC: BCI chair's tenure is for 2 years, can't be made 5 years by own resolution
Article Text:
The petitioners questioned the lavish spending of crores on felicitation functions

Petitioners question lavish spend

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: With two PILs heaping allegations against functioning of advocates regulatory body Bar Council of India and questioning legality of its Apr 2025 resolution giving a five-year term to chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra, Supreme Court Wednesday said no resolution can override the statutorily prescribed two-year term.A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said even if a BCI resolution generously gives a five-year term to the chairperson, his tenure ex-facie cannot exceed beyond 2027 notwithstanding the legality of the resolution.No resolution can alter the statutorily provided two-year tenure for the chairperson,” the bench said.The petitioners questioned the lavish spending of crores on felicitation functions, organising seminars and alleged misuse of Bar Council of India trust funds to open law colleges in states and demanded a high-level inquiry into the council’s affairs.The bench said the elections to state bar councils had been completed and directed the completion of co-option of women members by the high court chief justices concerned in consultation with newly elected members within two weeks.The entire composition of state bar councils, including co-opted women members, would be notified within a week thereafter.It said the newly formed state bar councils would elect their representative to BCI a week later to enable the latter to conduct fresh election of the chairperson and the vice-chairperson.Till then, the BCI governing body would act in a pro tem manner and not take any policy decision.On the bench’s suggestion, the council volunteered to invite the attorney general and the solicitor general to its meetings.Mishra has been chairperson of BCI since Nov 9, 2014.The petitioners asked whether a statutory authority entrusted with “regulating more than 20 lakh advocates, administering legal education, conducting the All India Bar Examination, exercising disciplinary jurisdiction, and safeguarding independence of the legal profession, can lawfully permit prolonged concentration of regulatory authority in the same hands through successive and substantially uncontested terms”.
Article Summary: Two PILs heaping allegations against functioning of advocates regulatory body Bar Council of India. Supreme Court Wednesday said no resolution can override the statutorily prescribed two-year term. The petitioners questioned the lavish spending of crores on felicitation functions.

Article Title: Nepal floods bring 'unusual' fish to Bihar, govt warns people not to eat or sell them

BETTIAH: Unidentified and unusual fish swept into the Gandak river and its floodplains by floodwaters from Nepal have prompted the Bihar govt to issue a safety advisory, asking residents of West Champaran and Gopalganj not to consume or trade in such fish until their identity and safety are confirmed.The fisheries division of the dairy, fisheries and animal resources department issued the caution on Tuesday after unusual fish were found in local water bodies and low-lying areas across the flood-hit Gandak basin.Floodwaters from Nepal have entered the Gandak system, inundating several areas of West Champaran and Gopalganj. The department said fish can be swept away from ponds, rivers and other water bodies during floods and carried over considerable distances. During this movement, they may come into contact with contaminated drains, dead animals and other pollutants, raising the risk of contamination by bacteria, viruses and fungi.“Do not consume any unidentified or unusual-looking fish. Until confirmation by the concerned department, an unfamiliar fish should not be considered fit for consumption,” the advisory said.Residents have also been asked not to buy or sell unfamiliar fish caught from floodwaters or assume an unusual-looking species is safe merely because it resembles a commonly eaten fish.Anyone developing vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, dizziness or breathing difficulty after consuming such fish has been advised to seek immediate medical attention.Wildlife Trust of India director Sameer Kumar Sinha said most fish swept into the Gandak in Bihar following the Nepal floods are believed to be ‘Bagarius bagarius’, commonly known as the goonch catfish and locally called “Gochita”.He said the large freshwater catfish is found in fast-flowing rivers of India, Nepal and parts of Southeast Asia. The carnivorous species feeds on smaller fish, crabs and other aquatic organisms and often hides among rocks in deep stretches with strong currents.Sinha said local communities consume the fish, but it spoils quickly after death and may pose health risks if eaten after deterioration. He urged people to follow the Bihar govt advisory and exercise caution. The species is listed by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) as threatened.

More intriguing is the fact - as coming out from the testimony of the official witnesses - that the amounts received in auction in excess of the appropriation to the loan accounts are still remaining with the bank.While granting a clean chit to the lone surviving accused bank official and terming the case a fabricated one, the bench said, "We are surprised that no attempt was made to find the legal heirs and pass on the money."Supreme Court asked the manager of Indian Bank's Anna Nagar Branch to produce records relating to the utilisation of the money received from the auction, and the title deeds of the properties mortgaged against loans. NEW DELHI: As two govt organisations took contradictory stands on commercial production of next-generation green firecrackers - with Council of Scientific and Industrial Research-NEERI approving new formulations and Central Pollution Control Board objecting - Centre Wednesday told Supreme Court that it intended to conduct fresh tests to assess the harmful impact of the use of barium.Additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati told a bench of Justices M M Sundresh and Augustine George Masih that govt, after consulting stakeholders, had decided to conduct the tests in New Delhi, Bhopal, Kolkata and Chennai.Centre had asked CSIR-NEERI to develop green/low-emission fireworks - with particulate matter (PM) emission reduction of more than 50% - in association with manufacturers. Tamil Nadu Fireworks and Amorces Manufacturers' Association (Tanfama) devised new-generation formulation crackers with a reduced quantity of barium salts/nitrates in combination with other oxidisers.In a report, CSIR-NEERI said with the new formulations, emission reductions achieved for PM10 and PM2.5 were between 45% and 60%, and recommended that the formulations for light-emission fireworks (such as flowerpots, sparklers, chakkars, pencils, twinkling stars and their hybrids) be considered for commercial production.It also approved the manufacture of 'joined crackers', known as 'ladis', which have been banned by a court order.The report said there was a reduction in PM emissions by approximately 30% and a reduction in solid waste generation by up to 32% for joined crackers.CPCB asked how barium nitrate could be used in crackers when it was banned by SC. "This court, vide order dated Oct 23, 2018, has expressly banned the use of barium salts in firecrackers and, therefore, any formulation involving barium compounds, even in reduced quantities, is in contravention of the said order," it said in its communication to govt."The reported reduction in PM10 and PM2.5 levels has not been comparatively assessed with (i) improved low-emission crackers and (ii) green crackers formulated entirely without barium, rendering the claim incomplete and inconclusive," it added.The petitioners, on whose plea polluting firecrackers were banned, submitted that the court had over the years passed eight orders to ban the use of barium and its use in cracker manufacturing could not be allowed.SC asked Centre to get suggestions from experts, saying the court had no expertise in these matters.

TRISHULI BAZAAR (NUWAKOT, NEPAL): India assured support for complete reconstruction of flood-ravaged Tribhuvan Trishuli Secondary School in Bidur, two days after TOI reported that the institution was seeking New Delhi's help to rebuild on higher, safer ground.The assurance came less than a week after around 900 students on campus escaped the Aug 26 flash flood following an emergency evacuation, while hundreds more travelling to school were stopped from entering the danger zone. The school had 1,643 students enrolled.Indian ambassador to Nepal Naveen Srivastava met the school's principal Rajendra Dawadi Tuesday. Srivastava recalled the institution's long association with India, including construction of its newer building through Indian grant assistance. He said Dawadi's timely action had saved lives of over 1,600 schoolchildren. TOI had earlier reported how around 900 students were inside the school when warnings came, while buses carrying hundreds of others were stopped before reaching the danger zone.Dawadi told TOI after the meeting with Srivastava on Wednesday: "We are deeply grateful to India for the reassurance and for standing with us at this difficult time.The assurance has given the entire school community hope at a time when we are trying to restart classes and also looking for a safe location for a permanent campus. Our entire school infrastructure has been destroyed, so our immediate priority is to bring the students back to classrooms. "The flood has swept away virtually the entire campus, including its 18-room, three-storey academic block. The school's two buses were among the few assets left. Two staffers - non-teaching employee Chulrim Lama and secondary teacher Santos Parihar - still remain missing.The school's links with India stretch back decades. Embassy of India records said Tribhuvan Trishuli Secondary School was established in 1951 and was designed by K I Singh, an Indian engineer who had come to Nepal for Trishuli Hydro Project. India later funded a new school building at a cost of NRs 25 million, or Nepalese Rs 2.5 crore, under India-Nepal Development Cooperation.Indian officials and local authorities inaugurated the building on Aug 2, 2022.India's latest assurance came as Nepal's private sector also mobilised assistance for schools and communities hit by the flood. Chaudhary Foundation, CSR arm of Chaudhary Group, announced immediate assistance to help Tribhuvan Trishuli Secondary School restart classes from a temporary location.Dawadi said restoring a Bailey bridge would make restart easier. Article Title: ‘Not democratically elected’: SC says Manan Kumar Mishra only ‘pro tem’ BCI chairman till fresh election
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday said Bar Council of India (BCI) chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra was only a “pro tem Chairman” until a freshly constituted BCI elects its office-bearers, and directed that major policy decisions be taken in consultation with the Attorney General for India and the Solicitor General, who are permanent ex-officio BCI members.A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant and comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said Mishra could oversee the BCI's day-to-day functioning but could not be treated as a democratically elected office-bearer once the newly elected state bar councils complete the process of constituting a fresh BCI.“You should also bear in mind that you are like a pro tem chairman till a fresh election of the Bar Council of India, pursuant to the elections already conducted in the state bar councils, takes place,” Justice Bagchi told senior advocate Guru Krishnakumar, appearing for the BCI chairman, according to LiveLaw.“So, it is not a situation where he is democratically elected and continues to be so. His term is co-terminus with the elections which are imminent,” the judge said.The court said the existing arrangement could continue for routine administrative work but stressed that institutional checks would apply to policy decisions.“In such situations, day-to-day functioning can be left to the existing arrangement. However, when a policy decision is taken, the participation of a permanent ex officio member acting independently, such as the Attorney General, is necessary,” Justice Bagchi remarked orally, PTI said.The bench also said it was not endorsing Mishra's continued tenure.“We are not placing any stamp of approval upon the existing arrangement. It is apparent that the present chairperson can continue only until a fresh election to the Bar Council of India takes place pursuant to the state bar council elections already conducted,” it said.The observations came while the court heard pleas challenging Mishra's continued occupation of the BCI chairperson's post and the legal basis for extending his tenure until 2030.Senior advocate Madhavi Divan, appearing for the petitioners, said Mishra was unanimously elected chairman for a term from April 17, 2025 to April 16, 2030. She also challenged a resolution extending the tenure of the chairman and vice-chairman from three years to five years despite rules prescribing a two-year term.Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for one of the petitioners, questioned the creation of the Bar Council of India Trust for Promotion of Education, Legal and Professional Reforms and Improvement in Research.Sankaranarayanan alleged that its deed made 11 managing trustees “original and permanent trustees”. The bench questioned how elected members could appoint themselves as perpetual trustees.“The Bar Council of India is a juristic entity. That entity has created a trust from its assets through the elected members who constituted the Council. Can those elected members make themselves permanent trustees of those assets when the composition of the corporate entity that settled the trust is itself determined through elections?” it asked.The court directed the newly constituted state bar councils to elect their office-bearers and representatives to the BCI within three weeks of notification of their composition. The matter will be heard next on September 23.
Article Summary: BCI chief Manan Kumar Mishra only ‘pro tem’ till fresh election, Supreme Court says. Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said Mishra could oversee the BCI's day-to-day functioning but could not be treated as a democratically elected office-bearer.

NEW DELHI: Climate change, deforestation, unplanned urbanisation and poor drainage are creating conditions for mosquitoes and other disease-carrying vectors to spread into new areas of the Northeast, a parliamentary health panel has warned, calling for targeted, technology-driven surveillance and prevention strategies.The Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and Family Welfare, in its report on vector-borne diseases in North-East India, said the region's difficult terrain, changing rainfall and temperature patterns, rapid urbanisation and gaps in healthcare access were contributing to the persistence and geographical expansion of these diseases.The numbers show a sharp rise in dengue in the region. Reported cases increased from 142 in 2014 to 19,761 in 2023, before falling to 7,186 in 2024. The report records 1,524 cases in 2025 through August, making it a partial-year figure and therefore not directly comparable with full-year totals.Chikungunya cases in the region increased from 3,493 in 2023 to 3,991 in 2024, an increase of about 14.3%.The panel said dengue and chikungunya are increasingly urban concerns, driven by urbanisation, water-storage practices, poor waste management, climate change and population movement.Sikkim recorded the highest incidence among Northeast states, with 374 dengue cases in 2024. Using the state’s revised population estimate, the dengue incidence was 57.9 per lakh. Sikkim also reported 1,863 chikungunya cases, with an incidence of 291.2 per lakh in 2024.Malaria, however, presents a more mixed picture. Across India, the number of high-burden districts with an Annual Parasite Index above one fell from 155 in 2015 to 37 in 2024. In the Northeast, 16 districts in Arunachal Pradesh and six in Nagaland have reported zero indigenous malaria cases for the past three years.Japanese encephalitis remains another concern, particularly in Assam and other northeastern states. The report records 885 JE cases in the Northeast in 2024, compared with 709 in 2023. Nationally, the JE fatality rate fell substantially, from 17.6% in 2014 to 7.1% in 2024.The panel recommended real-time surveillance through a dedicated Northeast vector-borne disease portal and AI-based early-warning systems to predict hotspots, along with mobile health units, pre-monsoon camps, rapid-response teams, stronger labs and dedicated NESIDS funding for high-risk areas. It also called for disease-specific treatment protocols for severe dengue and other complications, a Regional Entomology Training Hub, and greater use of climate modelling and digital reporting. The panel flagged a data gap too: vector-borne disease data are not separately collected for tribal, rural and urban populations, and recommended doing so for more targeted interventions.
Article Summary: Climate change, deforestation, unplanned urbanisation and poor drainage are creating conditions for mosquitoes and other disease-carrying vectors to spread into new areas of the Northeast. The Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and Family Welfare said the region's difficult terrain, changing rainfall and temperature patterns were contributing to the persistence and geographical expansion of these diseases.

Article Title: AIMPLB to launch campaign for protection Constitution and Sharia

The All India Muslim Personal Law Board will launch a movement on Sept 17

NEW DELHI: The All India Muslim Personal Law Board will launch a movement on Sept 17 to mobilise public opinion for protection of the Constitution and 'Sharia', religious freedom and rights and dignity of citizens. The Board plans to start the campaign from Jantar Mantar in Delhi and reach out to all faiths over three months.In a statement, the board said that as part of the campaign, a charter of demands will be submitted to the President of India Droupadi Murmu through governors in each state. Besides these issues, the charter will also include demands concerning elimination of hate crimes, prevention of unlawful demolitions, protection of Waqf properties and religious places, and equal enforcement of the law.The Board also proposes to bring out a ‘White Paper’ documenting incidents involving discrimination against Muslims, constitutional and human rights violations and release a comprehensive declaration on the issue of lynching.It said over the past several years conditions have emerged wherein vulnerable and marginalised sections, particularly Muslims, have been subjected to discriminatory treatment.The Board listed concerns ranging from extra-legal bulldozer demolitions, attempts to undermine Muslim Personal Law through Uniform Civil Code to undermining the beliefs of the minority community by making the singing of all six verses of Vande Mataram compulsory, as serious challenges to the Constitution of India, social harmony and national unity.Meanwhile, on the controversy following Kerala’s grand mufti Sheikh Abubakr Ahmad’s comments that women should remain confined to their homes and should not enter the public sphere, arguing that Islam prescribed the purdah system to protect their dignity, AIMPLB spokesperson SQR Ilyas objected to the remarks.Noting that Islam nowhere calls for women to be kept confined to the House for their safety, Ilyas said that the interpretation made by Ahmad is “not correct” and is therefore “misplaced.”He also cited the board’s profile highlighting that there were nearly 30 women in the AIMPLB and asserted that the board was fully in support of the idea of enabling Muslim women to progress which is in keeping with the Islamic teachings.

Article Title: Year-wise plan to implement Samudra Manthan in works
Article Text:
Petroleum minister Hardeep Puri reviewed the action taken on decisions from two brainstorming sessions on the rollout of the scheme, which received Cabinet’s approval, said officials. (Photo: IANS)

NEW DELHI: Government is likely to finalise a year-wise plan soon for drilling, seismic surveys and rig deployment under Samudra Manthan, a Rs 84,084-crore national programme aimed at stepping up oil and gas exploration in India’s offshore basins and reducing dependence on energy imports.Officials said petroleum minister Hardeep Puri recently reviewed the action taken on decisions from two brainstorming sessions held in Gurgaon in Haryana and Duliajan in Assam, on the rollout of the scheme, which received Cabinet’s approval last month.The year-wise roadmap will help government carry out exploration and production activities in a concerted manner across Krishna-Godavari (KG), Mahanadi, Andaman and Cauvery basins and ensure systematic utilisation of funds, an official said.The scheme will fund acquisition, processing and interpretation of seismic data, scientific drilling in frontier basins, accelerated exploration in deepwater and ultra-deepwater blocks, and development of shared offshore production and evacuation infrastructure.While Rs 43,200 crore has been earmarked for drilling 60 exploratory deepwater wells over five years, Rs 28,534 crore has been allocated for acquisition of 2D and 3D seismic data, Rs 10,000 crore for common infrastructure hubs and Rs 2,000 crore for an oil and gas manufacturing and services zone.India’s annual crude oil requirement is around 256 million tonnes (MT), of which nearly 88 per cent is imported. Domestic crude oil production from 26 sedimentary basins is estimated at around 28 MT. With domestic output stagnating even as demand continues to rise, government has been looking to step up exploration to improve energy security and reduce import dependence.Samudra Manthan is expected to add more than 600 million metric tonnes of oil equivalent (MMTOE) to the country’s hydrocarbon reserves and boost domestic production of crude oil and natural gas.Officials said government has implemented a series of upstream sector reforms over the past decade, including opening up almost the entire offshore acreage for exploration, changes to legal and contractual framework, and strengthening National Data Repository. Samudra Manthan would complement these reforms by providing public funding for offshore exploration and facilitating the deployment of advanced technologies, they said.The scheme also includes dedicated provisions for digital programme management, capacity building, technology adoption, stakeholder engagement and international outreach, creating an integrated ecosystem to accelerate offshore exploration and production in the country.
Article Summary: Government is likely to finalise a year-wise plan soon for drilling, seismic surveys and rig deployment under Samudra Manthan. The scheme is aimed at stepping up oil and gas exploration in India’s offshore basins and reducing dependence on energy imports.

Article Title: PM Modi repeats call to 'shun unnecessary gold buys, foreign weddings & holidays'
Article Text:
PM Modi on Tuesday lauded Indian economy's resilience during a period of global crises

NEW DELHI: Buoyed by the better-than-expected GDP growth, PM Modi on Tuesday lauded Indian economy's resilience during a period of global crises. He again pushed for swadeshi goods and urged citizens to shun overseas weddings, foreign vacations and avoid unnecessary gold purchases at a time when imports remain elevated due to high commodity prices in the wake of the West Asia conflict.His appeal against buying gold also puts to rest speculation around import duties being reviewed by govt. In fact, Centre and RBI are keeping a close watch on shipments. Since Jan, both quantity of gold and value of imports have increased. Since Modi's first appeal in May, however, there has been a drop in quantity of imports but the value of imports is rising due to higher prices, albeit at a slower pace. At $3.5 a kg, the unit value of gold was 94% higher in June, but prices have moderated to $2.8 a kg, which was 47% more than a year ago.Since Modi’s first appeal in May, gold import quantity has dropped, but import value is rising due to higher prices, albeit slower. Prices moderated to $2.8 a kg, 47% more than a year ago.While gold remains an investment option for households, higher prices have deterred consumers from buying large quantities, with recycling of old jewellery also rising, industry executives said.Modi also mounted a withering attack on LoP Rahul Gandhi for spreading pessimism about growth, dismissing his criticism as “jhooth ki goonj”.This was Modi’s second reaction to the growth rate within 24 hours. His message mixed praise for people’s hard work with disdain for critics like Rahul and reiterated his call to citizens to avoid non-essential gold purchases and foreign trips.“We have to maintain this pace and keep growing and, for this, aatmanirbhar Bharat is essential,” he said in a selfie-video posted on Instagram.GDP grew at 7.8% in the April-June quarter, bringing relief to the NDA govt, which has been buffeted by the opposition parties, especially Congress under Rahul, over alleged misgovernance. Modi said, “There are people within India who are mired in despair, ‘jhooth ki goonj’, and are busy spreading pessimism everywhere.”Emphasising India’s feat, Modi said it came amid global conflicts and crises, causing supply-chain disruption. Since Covid in 2020, stability has remained elusive for the world but India is progressing at a fast pace, he added.Opposition has a right to criticise govt but especially Congress shouldn’t insult people by being incorrigible naysayers and call India a dead economy when data speaks otherwise, finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said.BJP played up Rahul’s dismissive comments about the economy to contrast them with India’s growth. Besides his dead economy jibe, Rahul claimed a crisis unseen in people’s lifetime would hit the economy. An economic tsunami was coming, he had said. Modi said his govt’s policy is right and intentions clear, calling upon people to work hard. India’s collective strength will take it to new heights. By emphasising swadeshi and self-reliance, people will bequeath a developed India to the young generation.At a press conference, BJP’s Ravi Shankar Prakash demanded Rahul apologise. As leader of opposition, Rahul’s comments carry weight, he said. The world has begun taking them lightly as he makes misleading remarks, while Pakistan plays them up.
Article Summary: PM Modi on Tuesday lauded Indian economy's resilience during a period of global crises. He again pushed for swadeshi goods and urged citizens to shun overseas weddings, foreign vacations and avoid unnecessary gold purchases. His appeal against buying gold also puts to rest speculation around import duties being reviewed by govt. Since Jan, both quantity of gold and value of imports have increased.

Article Title: Travis Kelce’s $1.5 million nonprofit faces scrutiny after records show $469,000 spent on management and $446,000 on charity
Article Text:
Travis Kelce(Image via Getty Images)

Travis Kelce nonprofit spending comes under scrutiny

Travis Kelce foundation says tax filings were incorrect

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Earlier this year, Travis Kelce ’s reputation for giving back was facing a setback after an investigation into the NFL players’ charitable foundations raised questions about how some donated money was spent. Kelce’s Eighty-Seven and Running Foundation raised more than $1.5 million between 2021 and 2024, yet its reported charity spending was notably lower than that of several other NFL-linked organizations.In January, 2026, according to federal tax records examined by The Arizona Republic, Eighty-Seven and Running reported about $1.5 million in revenue during the three-year period and roughly $1.1 million in expenses. About $446,000 was listed under charitable spending, while $469,000 was reported as management costs.That works out to about 41 cents of every dollar spent going toward charity based on the filings. Charity Navigator generally views nonprofits spending at least 70 cents of each dollar on programs as efficient, while CharityWatch uses 75 cents as a benchmark for high efficiency.The figures have drawn attention partly because of the foundation's ties to A&A Management Group.The company was co-founded by Travis Kelce’s longtime business managers, Aaron and André Eanes. Aaron Eanes also serves as the nonprofit’s executive director.Laurie Styron, executive director of CharityWatch, raised concerns about the structure after reviewing the records.“It appears to function more as an extension of the management company versus as an independent public charity,” said Laurie Styron, the executive director of CharityWatch, an independent charity watchdog group that reviewed the nonprofit’s tax filings for The Arizona Republic.“That’s not how charities work. It’s wrong.”Travis Kelce’s team disputes the picture presented by the filings. Aaron Eanes said the reported figures did not properly classify some operational expenses tied to charitable work.“Operational costs for charitable efforts were “mistakenly reported under management rather than allocated adequately to program services,” Eanes told The Republic, so the public records do not provide an accurate “indication of where the resources were truly directed.”.Eanes said the foundation has since changed its approach, adding that management fees fell sharply in 2024 and reached zero in 2025. He also said the organization plans to expand its board, bring in nonprofit advisers and improve its reporting practices.“Looking ahead, we are expanding our board of directors, bringing on advisers with nonprofit expertise, and restructuring our reporting processes to better reflect our actual program work. We are dedicated to ensuring this foundation operates at the highest standards.”The scrutiny comes as the NFL continues to highlight charitable work through the Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year program. Kelce has been nominated three times and has supported causes in both Kansas City and his hometown of Cleveland.Kelce's foundation’s reported numbers do not erase that community work, but they do highlight why financial transparency matters. For celebrity-led nonprofits, public trust depends not only on how much money is raised, but also on how clearly and responsibly that money reaches the people it is meant to help.
Article Summary: Travis Kelce’s Eighty-Seven and Running Foundation raised more than $1.5 million between 2021 and 2024, yet its reported charity spending was notably lower than that of several other NFL-linked organizations. The figures have drawn attention partly because of the foundation's ties to A&A Management Group. Kelce has been nominated three times for the Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year program.

Article Title: 'Intellectual dishonesty': SBI hits back at 2.6% GDP growth claim, says numbers compared incorrectly
Article Text:
SBI hits back at 2.6% GDP growth claim, says numbers were compared incorrectly

Dispute over the 2.6% figure

Real GDP growth would still be strong

Latest figures to be revised

The State Bank of India (SBI) has rejected claims that India’s nominal GDP growth in the first quarter of FY27 was only 2.6%, saying the figure came from comparing two different versions of the GDP data.The pushback came after former finance secretary Subhash Chandra Garg questioned the government’s reported 7.8% real GDP growth for Q1 FY27.Garg pointed to a revision in the previous year’s current-price GDP saying that Q1 FY26 GDP had been revised from around Rs 86 lakh crore to about Rs 80 lakh crore and argued that, without the revision, nominal growth would have been around 2.6%.Official data released by the ministry of statistics and programme implementation (MoSPI) showed real GDP growing 7.8% year-on-year in Q1 FY27. Real GDP at constant prices stood at an estimated Rs 81.36 lakh crore, up from Rs 75.46 lakh crore in Q1 FY26. Nominal GDP growth was reported at 10.3%.SBI said the 2.6% figure does not represent a valid comparison, rather it is "completely unsolicited and a sure sign of intellectual dishonesty.”The National Statistical Office (NSO) had estimated nominal GDP for Q1 FY26 at Rs 86.1 lakh crore when it released the quarterly figures on August 29, 2025.However, the August 31 release, prepared using the new GDP base year of 2022-23, revised the Q1 FY26 figure down to Rs 80 lakh crore.For Q1 FY27, nominal GDP was estimated at Rs 88.3 lakh crore.According to SBI, the 2.6% growth figure comes from comparing the latest Rs 88.3 lakh crore estimate with the older Rs 86.1 lakh crore figure for Q1 FY26, instead of using the revised number.“Some estimates are now ascribing a 2.6% growth in nominal GDP for the latest quarter instead of 10.3%, by calculating yearly growth rate using Rs 88.3 lakh crore (we call it A series in the adjacent table) over Rs 86.1 lakh crore (we call it C series). This is completely unsolicited and a sure sign of intellectual dishonesty,” SBI said.The bank said the latest Q1 FY27 figure should instead be compared with the revised Q1 FY26 figure under the new GDP series. That calculation gives nominal GDP growth of 9.7%.SBI also laid out an alternative comparison for those wanting to use the previous, unrevised Q1 GDP base. It said the Rs 88.3 lakh crore Q1 FY27 figure should be compared with Rs 80.4 lakh crore under the new base, rather than the old Rs 86.1 lakh crore estimate.“If anyone truly wants to compare current nominal GDP numbers over the previous unrevised base of Q1 GDP, then Rs 88.3 lakh crore (new base, A series) should be estimated over Rs 80.4 lakh crore (new base, B series), which comes out to 9.7% growth (as against 10.3%),” the report said.SBI said that the picture would remain positive even if nominal growth were calculated differently. It said that after adjusting the deflator under the alternative calculation, real GDP growth for Q1 FY27 would be 7.4%, compared with the officially released 7.8%.“Hypothetically, even with this nominal growth (by adjusting deflator), the real growth for Q1 FY27 would be 7.4% (as against released 7.8%), still good enough when looking at wall of exogenous challenges,” it said.The bank also stressed that GDP numbers are not final when they are first released. Quarterly estimates are revised over time and those revisions can move in either direction.SBI said that between FY22 and FY25, quarterly GDP data saw 25 upward revisions and 12 downward revisions.According to SBI, what made the latest revision different was that the National Accounts Statistics directly incorporated revised figures from previous years into the quarterly data.The bank said this was done to make the figures more transparent and to bring them in line with base revisions in the Consumer Price Index (CPI), Index of Industrial Production (IIP), Wholesale Price Index (WPI) and Producer Price Index (PPI).“This is perfectly legitimate,” SBI said.It added that aligning the bases helps keep GDP deflators and volume estimates consistent with the updated price and production indices.The bank also pointed out that the Q1 FY27 GDP estimate released in August 2026 is itself not final. The figure will go through further revisions and is expected to be finalised only by February 2029.“Revisions are part and parcel of a GDP number,” SBI said.SBI also rejected the claim that the change in the GDP base year had increased the size of India’s nominal GDP. According to the bank, the latest base-year revision had actually resulted in a lower nominal GDP size.
Article Summary: State Bank of India rejects claims that India's nominal GDP growth in the first quarter of FY27 was only 2.6%. Official data released by the ministry of statistics and programme implementation (MoSPI) showed real GDP growing 7.8% year-on-year in Q1 FY27. Nominal GDP growth was reported at 10.3%.
