Article Title: Indian Navy SATCOM : Indian Navy eyes indigenous SATCOM terminals to boost network-centric warfare
Article Text:
The Indian Navy is seeking to enhance network warfare capability through improved satellite communication technology. (Image credit: Indian Navy)

India Project 18 Destroyer: Japan’s Maya Technology Could Change India’s Navy

In the middle of a modernisation drive, the Indian Navy is seeking to improve its network centric warfare capability. The navy has floatted an Expression of Interest (EoI) for the development of indigenous ship-based satellite communication (SATCOM) terminals designed to work with its latest satellite, the GSAT-7R. The project, seeks a domestically developed and industry funded SATCOM system. The indigenously developed advanced C-band and Ku-band terminals will let warships maintain secure voice, data and video links even while operating thousands of kilometres out at sea.The Navy has been leaning on satellite communication since 2013, when GSAT-7 Rukmini first went into service. This satellite provided the fleet with a single secure network. This capability was significantly expanded with the launch of GSAT-7R, this satellite launched in November last year extends secure communication coverage to roughly 2,000 kilometres across the Indian Ocean Region. What the Navy wants now is for the ship-based terminals that talk through this satellite.The enhanced capability will allow the navy to strengthen its network warfare capability. This capability links different ship and aircraft into a single shared operational picture, so commanders across the force can see the same real-time data on enemy dispositions, own-force locations and emerging threats.Rather than each platform fighting in isolation the entire fleet is fused and distributed instantly across the network, letting any unit engage a target even if it wasn't the one that spotted the target.This capability was first demonstrated by the navy during Exercise TROPEX in 2014. Roughly 60 warships and 75 aircraft were connected into one network via the GSAT-7 Rukmini satellite, this resulted in faster decision-making and better coordination across a dispersed fleet. This provided the fleet with the ability to have different ships act as the sensor and the shooter platform.The system relies on Rukmini Terminals, the new systems are meant to reduce mechanical components wherever possible, improving reliability in harsh maritime conditions marked by constant rolling, pitching and yawing, salt-laden air, high winds and vibration. The programme will begin with three prototypes, a large C-band terminal, a large Ku-band terminal and a smaller Ku-band terminal, before moving to series production of around 30 units in total. As with other Make-II projects, companies will bear the full development cost themselves, with a minimum 50% indigenous content mandated across both hardware and embedded software, as per the EoI.Testing requirements are notably rigorous, including three-axis motion table trials to simulate real sea conditions and validate that the terminal can hold a stable satellite link, alongside evaluation at the Space Applications Centre in Ahmedabad and a mandatory vulnerability assessment clearance before integration into the Navy's network. The project has been reserved for MSMEs for now, with startups and consortiums of up to five members also eligible to participate. Companies have until 22 September to raise queries, with the EoI submission deadline set for 24 October, followed by a 104-week window to develop working prototypes.
Article Summary: The Indian Navy is seeking to enhance network warfare capability through improved satellite communication technology. The project, seeks a domestically developed and industry funded SATCOM system. The indigenously developed advanced C-band and Ku-band terminals will let warships maintain secure voice, data and video links while operating thousands of kilometres out at sea.

Article Title: Bengal UCC likely to replace 13 marriage Acts with a single law
Article Text:
West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari

Codes that may be substituted





KOLKATA: At least 13 marriage acts are likely to be replaced by a single law focusing on gender equality and religion-neutrality under Bengal’s proposed Uniform Civil Code (UCC).The UCC, being drafted by a committee which will hold its first meeting in Delhi on Thursday, will replace religion-specific personal laws with a unified legal framework governing marriage, divorce, maintenance, succession and guardianship across all communities. Scheduled Tribes will remain outside the code’s ambit.A source said, “At least 13 marriage acts (see graphic) will be revoked under the proposed UCC and replaced by a single act. The primary emphasis will be on gender equality, followed by religion-neutrality. The new act will not interfere with cultural practices, attire or traditional rituals.”The 13 acts likely to be replaced are Indian Divorce Act, 1869; Indian Christian Marriage Act, 1872; Bengal Muhammadan Marriages and Divorces Registration Act, 1876; Anand Marriage Act, 1909; Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act, 1936; Arya Marriage Validation Act, 1937; Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act, 1937; Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939; Special Marriage Act, 1954; Hindu Marriage Act, 1955; Foreign Marriage Act, 1969; Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986; and Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019.The acts, applied on the basis of faith, interfaith status and overseas location, govern matrimonial rites, civil unions and divorces.Under the proposed UCC, all marriages must be registered with designated state authorities within a specified deadline.There will be no out-of-court divorces. Grounds for divorce will be identical for both partners and the spouses will have equal rights regarding maintenance and alimony. Traditional practices of separation, such as Nikah halala, will be abolished,” the source said.The proposed code mandates live-in partners to register their partnership, failing which they will face penalties. “This will prevent fraud and also ensure legal protection for both partners as well as children born out of live-in relationships,” the source said. “There will be no provision for polygamy or bigamy under the Bengal UCC. Child marriage will be banned regardless of religion.”In matters of succession, sons and daughters will enjoy equal rights to ancestral property. Adoption and testamentary wills, too, will be religion-neutral and gender-equal.Osman Mallick, a lawyer and member of the committee drafting the UCC, said, “The panel will have its first meeting in Delhi tomorrow to formulate a comprehensive roadmap for the Bengal UCC. Currently, we are finalising preliminary administrative work.”
Article Summary: At least 13 marriage acts are likely to be replaced by a single law focusing on gender equality and religion-neutrality. Scheduled Tribes will remain outside the code’s ambit. Under the proposed UCC, all marriages must be registered with designated state authorities within a specified deadline.

Article Title: 3 pose as cops, force bizman to pay Rs 50L to 'settle CBI case'
Article Text:
The accused allegedly demanded Rs 15 crore for the settlement and kept threatening the victim with jail time if he did not pay up





Ghaziabad: Three men have been arrested for allegedly extorting money from an Indirapuram businessman by posing as senior govt officials. The accused allegedly threatened to arrest the businessman and shut down his firm unless he paid Rs 15 crore to settle an alleged CBI notice.On Tuesday, the businessman, Vikas Mittal, filed a complaint at Indirapuram police station alleging that five men had falsely identified themselves as senior-ranking CBI and NIA officers. They told him they could ‘settle’ a case that the agencies had filed against his firm and demanded money from him. Mittal told cops he had already paid Rs 50 lakh to the accused.Based on CCTV footage and inputs from informers, a joint operation was conducted by SWAT, the surveillance team of the trans-Hindon zone and a team from Indirapuram police station. They arrested three men — Ankit Dwivedi (36), a resident of Vasant Kunj; Anil Pratap Singh (64), a resident of Greater Noida West; and Siddharth Jain (34), a resident of Pitampura — on Wednesday. They recovered Rs 1.9 lakh and seized three mobile phones and a diary from them. Efforts are underway to arrest the two others, police said.Deputy commissioner of police (city and trans-Hindon) Dhawal Jaiswal said the men allegedly told police during interrogation that the firm’s manager, Yogesh, had allegedly discussed with one of the accomplices, Salman, that the company he worked at had allegedly been served with a notice.He claimed he had contacts with senior officials in various govt departments and offered to get the matter ‘settled’.Police said Salman then introduced Yogesh to another accused, Siddharth Jain. Jain finally introduced Yogesh to Anil Pratap Singh. Singh posed as a senior-ranking officer and told the manager that he could get the notice resolved. He also convinced Yogesh that his employer, Vikas Mittal, could face arrest if the matter was not settled immediately.The accused allegedly demanded Rs 15 crore for the purported settlement. Police said Singh subsequently contacted firm owner Vikas Mittal and repeatedly threatened him with action and imprisonment in connection with the notice, allegedly collecting money from him.According to the police, Singh later sent his son Aniket alias Kabir, along with Ankit Dwivedi, to collect money from Mittal. The accused allegedly intimidated the complainant and jointly carried out the extortion Aniket alias Kabir and Salman, both named as accused in the case, are currently absconding. Police have formed teams to trace and arrest them. Further investigation is underway, including verification of the arrested suspects’ criminal records.
Article Summary: Three men arrested for allegedly extorting money from an Indirapuram businessman by posing as senior govt officials. The accused allegedly threatened to arrest the businessman and shut down his firm unless he paid Rs 15 crore to settle an alleged CBI notice. Police recovered Rs 1.9 lakh and seized three mobile phones and a diary from them.

Article Title: Maharashtra to decide fate of Ola, Uber and Rapido operations after Sept 4 meeting
Article Text:
File photo

Pune:





The state transport department will take a final call on whether Ola Uber and Rapido can continue operating cabs in Maharashtra , after meeting representatives of the aggregators and consulting chief minister Devendra Fadnavis on Sept 4The deadline for obtaining licences under the state’s new cab aggregator policy ended on Sept 1. Transport minister Pratap Sarnaik said none of the three aggregators had secured a licence to operate in the state.“During the meeting, we will ask them why they could not secure a licence. We will also consult the CM on the issue. The cab aggregator policy was introduced last month, and the aggregators should have secured their licences by now. They were given ample time,” Sarnaik said.In Pune, Uber and Rapido had applied for licences to operate e-bike taxis, while only Rapido had sought a licence for cab operations. However, none had been granted a licence so far, Pune RTO officer Archana Gaikwad said.A senior RTO official said the local office was awaiting directions from the state transport department before taking any action against the aggregators.“If we receive directions to initiate action, it will be done. This could mean that aggregator cabs will not be allowed to operate. At present, we have not received any such order from the higher authorities,” the RTO official said.Gaikwad had earlier said the applications submitted by the aggregators were under scrutiny and that they would have to fulfil all requirements under the policy for both cab and e-bike taxi operations.“In both cases, the aggregators need to fulfil all the requirements, failing which the applications are bound to be rejected. The process could take time,” she had said.Meanwhile, commuters continue to complain about cab drivers allegedly demanding fares higher than those displayed on aggregator apps, with many saying the issue has persisted for nearly two years.“Commuters have been facing this problem for close to two years, and there is still no relief. Why is it so difficult for the state govt to regulate cabs in the city? In other cities, these cabs are operating without such problems,” said Siddharth Kumar, a daily commuter.
Article Summary: The deadline for obtaining licences under the state’s new cab aggregator policy ended on Sept 1. Transport minister Pratap Sarnaik said none of the three aggregators had secured a licence to operate in the state. In Pune, Uber and Rapido had applied for licences to operate e-bike taxis. However, none had been granted a licence so far.

Article Title: 'Not educated enough to calculate new rate’: Auto drivers, commuters clash over missing revised fare chart in Pune
Article Text:
Pune's commuters are navigating a maze of confusion and disputes as new autorickshaw fares lead to overcharging





PUNE: For Mohammadwadi resident Shilpa Patedar, a trip from her home to JM Road on Tuesday turned into a frustrating tussle over the autorickshaw fare.“The auto driver told me that fares had increased and demanded Rs320. The fare from my place to JM Road by meter is usually Rs180-190. When I asked why he was not operating by the meter, he said it had not been calibrated according to the new fare structure. I then asked for a fare chart, but he said he did not have one. When I asked how he had calculated Rs320, he started explaining some random calculation. I eventually booked a cab after the argument and paid less,” said the homemaker.Confusion over the revised autorickshaw fare, effective from Sept 1, has been compounded by the absence of fare charts with most drivers. The lack of clarity has fuelled arguments, mistrust and allegations of overcharging among commuters.Pune RTO assured last month that autorickshaw drivers would receive hard copies of the revised fare chart, which they could show passengers until meters were recalibrated. However, many drivers said they were yet to receive the charts, making it difficult for them to quote the correct fare.“What are we supposed to do? Meter calibration takes time and requires us to visit the RTO.Until then, we are unable to quote the exact fare. Many drivers are not educated enough to calculate the fare accurately based on the distance travelled,” said an auto driver.“We have heard that some union office-bearers have been given copies of the fare chart, but we don’t know how these will be distributed. In many cases, drivers are refusing long trips or are forced to charge passengers according to the old fares,” he added.Pune regional transport officer Archana Gaikwad said unions had been given the new fare chart for distribution. “They need to photocopy the same and distribute it. It doesn’t take a lot of time. Also, we have sent the same to different newspapers for publication so that commuters can see the same and autorickshaw drivers too can keep a copy,” Gaikwad said.A Pune RTO official said meter calibration had begun and drivers had been given six months to complete the process. “Till then, the tariff card can be used to calculate fares. Unions need to ensure that every driver has a copy. RTO will conduct random checks to verify meter calibration and take action against overcharging and fleecing,” the official said.Nitin Pawar, general secretary of the Rickshaw Panchayat autorickshaw union, said the RTO had provided 10 copies of the fare chart to different unions.“Distribution of fare chart will begin from Wednesday. We are charging drivers Rs25 for a copy. There are a large number of drivers, so we are working out a systematic way to distribute the charts at the earliest,” he said.Kalyaninagar working professional Ashish Balke said drivers had been demanding substantially higher fares. “The fare from my home to my workplace in Vimannagar is a maximum of Rs100. On Tuesday, three autorickshaw drivers demanded Rs210, citing the revised fares. But none could explain how they had arrived at the amount. Getting an aggregator autorickshaw or cab is not always easy. I eventually agreed to pay Rs160 as I had to travel urgently,” he said.With around 1.45 lakh autorickshaws registered in Pune, commuters fear the confusion could persist. “There is no end to the hassles faced by commuters. With six months given for calibration, drivers could fleece passengers. RTO should have mandated that drivers charge the old fares until they receive the revised rate cards,” said Magarpatta resident Madhav Ghatge.
Article Summary: Confusion over the revised autorickshaw fare, effective from Sept 1, has been compounded by the absence of fare charts with most drivers. The lack of clarity has fuelled arguments, mistrust and allegations of overcharging among commuters. “There is no end to the hassles faced by commuters. With six months given for calibration, drivers could fleece passengers,” said Madhav Ghatge.

Article Title: Air India Express Varanasi-Delhi flight makes precautionary landing in Lucknow after smoke alert
Article Text:
Air India Express (File Photo)





LUCKNOW: Air India Express flight IX 1253, operating from Varanasi to Delhi, made a precautionary landing at Lucknow airport on Thursday morning after the pilots received a smoke indication from the aircraft's aft cargo compartment.According to an official source, the pilots reported that the aircraft's sensors had detected smoke in the cargo bay. They subsequently requested permission to make a precautionary landing at Chaudhary Charan Singh International Airport in Lucknow.The aircraft landed safely at 8.52 am, following which the airport emergency response team reached the site and conducted a visual inspection. No smoke was observed during the inspection.The aircraft was parked at a designated stand at the airport. Passenger deplaning began at 9.02 am, and all passengers were safely evacuated from the aircraft. The passengers were deboarded to facilitate a detailed inspection of the aircraft.In a statement, Lucknow International Airport Limited (LIAL), a subsidiary of Adani Airport Holdings Limited, said all 155 passengers and crew members on board were safe."Air India Express flight IX 1253 (Varanasi–Delhi) reported a smoke indication in the aft cargo compartment and made a precautionary landing at Lucknow Airport at 0852 hrs," the airport operator said."The aircraft landed safely, following which the airport emergency response team conducted a visual inspection. No smoke was observed," it added.The aircraft remained parked at the Lucknow airport bay after the passengers were deplaned.The cause of the smoke indication was not immediately known. A detailed inspection of the aircraft and its systems is expected to determine the reason for the alert. No passenger or crew member was reported injured in the incident.
Article Summary: Air India Express flight IX 1253, operating from Varanasi to Delhi, made a precautionary landing at Lucknow airport. The pilots received a smoke indication from the aircraft's aft cargo compartment. The aircraft landed safely at 8.52 am, following which the airport emergency response team reached the site.

Article Title: Tamil Nadu to build new assembly, secretariat complex in Chennai
Article Text:
Tamil Nadu CM Vijay





CHENNAI: Tamil Nadu will construct a new building complex housing the state Legislative Assembly and Secretariat in Chennai, at an estimated cost of Rs 1,200 crore. The complex will come up over an area of 20 lakh sq ft and will incorporate modern facilities and infrastructure.The proposed complex will have fire safety systems, facilities for persons with disabilities and modern security infrastructure. Adequate parking facilities will also be provided.The complex will include modern facilities for state government departments, public service centres and officials. The plan is to bring all government departments together at a single location, according to the announcement.The new complex is being planned as a modern government facility, with infrastructure aimed at improving public access as well as the functioning of government offices.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu will construct a new building complex housing the state Legislative Assembly and Secretariat in Chennai. The complex will come up over an area of 20 lakh sq ft and will incorporate modern facilities and infrastructure. The proposed complex will have fire safety systems, facilities for persons with disabilities and modern security infrastructure.

Article Title: Tamil Nadu to set up Olympic City, Motor Sports City: All you need to know
Article Text:
Tamil Nadu CM Vijay





CHENNAI: Tamil Nadu is set to establish an Olympic City and a Motor Sports City as part of its plans to create modern sports infrastructure and promote sports-related activities in the state.The Tamil Nadu Olympic City will have international-standard sports arenas, a High Performance Training Centre and accommodation facilities for sportspersons and coaches.It aims to provide better training and competition facilities and develop athletes capable of competing at national and international levels.A separate Motor Sports City will have a state-of-the-art motorsports complex and supporting infrastructure. Facilities will be created to host Formula 1, Formula 2, Formula 3 and Formula 4 races.It will also provide training opportunities and help identify and develop young motorsport talent.The Motor Sports City is expected to attract leading motor racing and car manufacturing companies to the state. The project is also expected to create opportunities in tourism, employment and related economic activities.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu set to establish an Olympic City and a Motor Sports City. The state wants to create modern sports infrastructure and promote sports-related activities. Tamil Nadu Olympic City will have international-standard sports arenas, a High Performance Training Centre and accommodation facilities for sportspersons.

Article Title: ‘Mayday emergency’: IndiGo Doha-Bengaluru flight diverts to Muscat after pilot falls ill mid-air
Article Text:
IndiGo flight (Representative image)





MUMBAI: An IndiGo flight from Doha to Bengaluru was diverted to Muscat on Thursday after one of its pilots was reportedly incapacitated mid-flight, prompting the aircraft to declare a Mayday emergency, said sources.The A320neo aircraft operating flight 6E 1302 took off from Doha at 3am, about an hour behind schedule, according to data from a flight-tracking website. Less than two hours later, the aircraft turned towards Muscat to carry out an approach and landing.Pilot incapacitation is treated as a serious in-flight emergency, as it means one of the pilots becomes unable to continue performing their duties.Aircraft such as those in the Airbus A320 family are operated by two pilots on the flight deck. If one becomes incapacitated, the other pilot can continue flying the aircraft.However, this would mean single-handedly managing all the duties normally shared between the two pilots on the flight deck, including flying and monitoring the aircraft, navigating, communicating with air traffic control, managing the aircraft’s systems and responding to abnormal or emergency situations.Since this can significantly increase the workload on the remaining pilot, pilot incapacitation is treated as an emergency.It can prompt the crew to divert to a suitable nearby airport, where the incapacitated pilot can receive medical attention and the flight can continue with a replacement crew.In a statement, IndiGo confirmed that the diversion was necessitated by an urgent requirement for medical attention for one operating crew member.The crew member was attended to by a medical team after landing and was reported to be feeling better, the airline added.The airline said an alternate aircraft and a new set of crew had been arranged to continue the journey to Bengaluru. Passengers waiting at Muscat were being provided refreshments and regular updates, it said.
Article Summary: IndiGo flight from Doha to Bengaluru was diverted to Muscat on Thursday. One of its pilots was reportedly incapacitated mid-flight, prompting the aircraft to declare a Mayday emergency. The crew member was attended to by a medical team after landing and was reported to be feeling better.

Article Title: How Rs 4.36 lakh shortfall led to discovery of Rs 7.4 crore fake notes in UP PNB bank vault
Article Text:
A cash shortfall at a Punjab National Bank currency chest revealed a counterfeit currency racket





SAHARANPUR: A cash shortfall of Rs 4.36 lakh in a remittance sent to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has led to the discovery of an alleged Rs 7.4 crore counterfeit currency racket inside a Punjab National Bank (PNB) currency chest in Uttar Pradesh's Saharanpur, prompting police to investigate whether bank insiders helped replace genuine notes with fake ones.Police have registered an FIR against bank officials and private individuals, while a Special Investigation Team (SIT) has been formed to probe how genuine currency worth Rs 7.4 crore allegedly disappeared from the vault and was replaced with counterfeit notes.The fraud came to light after a cash remittance dispatched to the RBI on Aug 10 was found to be short by Rs 4.36 lakh, according to PNB chief deputy manager Nisha Singh. The discrepancy prompted a detailed audit, during which investigators allegedly uncovered a large quantity of counterfeit currency in the bank's money vault.“The inquiry is in progress, and once we have complete details and evidence against everyone involved, the findings will be made public. The final tally of fake currency is still being verified as counting continues,” Singh said.The FIR was registered at Sadar police station on a complaint filed by PNB nodal officer Arun Kumar Chaubey. It names senior divisional manager Ravi Kumar and currency chest managers Sushil Sharma and Amit Kumar as primary suspects.In a parallel development, a separate report was filed against a housekeeper, Vishal Kumar, over what officials described as a “distinct cash shortfall” at the bank.Saharanpur DIG Abhishek said an SIT had been constituted to investigate the case and identify everyone involved in the alleged operation.“An SIT has been constituted and an FIR filed against those allegedly involved. Counting is in progress. Following a detailed inquiry, the embezzled currency will be recovered,” he said.Investigators are now examining bank transaction records, audit ledgers and CCTV footage from the currency chest to determine how the counterfeit notes allegedly entered the heavily secured vault and whether the operation involved insiders.The SIT is also trying to establish when the genuine currency was allegedly replaced, how long the counterfeit notes remained undetected and whether more people were involved in what investigators suspect could be a carefully planned operation.With the final count of counterfeit notes still under verification, the probe is expected to focus heavily on access to the currency chest and the movement of cash within the bank, as police attempt to unravel how an initial Rs 4.36 lakh discrepancy exposed an alleged Rs 7.4 crore currency swap.
Article Summary: A cash shortfall of Rs 4.36 lakh in a remittance sent to the Reserve Bank of India has led to the discovery of an alleged Rs 7.4 crore counterfeit currency racket. Police have registered an FIR against bank officials and private individuals. A Special Investigation Team (SIT) has been formed to probe how genuine currency disappeared from the vault.

Article Title: Mallikarjun Kharge slams PM Narendra Modi's 'PR on economy', cites unemployment and inflation
Article Text:
PM Narendra Modi and Mallikarjun Kharge (File Photo)





NEW DELHI: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Tuesday launched a sharp attack on Prime Minister Narendra Modi after he hailed India's 7.8 per cent GDP growth , saying the story of the PM's "PR on economy" has been one of "lights, camera and inaction."Responding to a video posted by Modi praising the country's economic performance, Kharge alleged that the government's claims did not reflect the realities faced by ordinary citizens."Lights. Camera and INACTION. This is the story of Modi ji's PR when it comes to the Economy," Kharge said on X."Narendra Modi ji, You are saying that the country is celebrating GDP Growth.You may have that luxury, but the Aam Aadmi does NOT! Our Common people are burdened by 3 'U's and YOU are responsible for that! 3 'U's --> Unprecedented Unemployment, Unbearable Price Rise & Unbridled Inequality!" Kharge said, as PTI reported.The Congress chief claimed unemployment was at a 50-year high and that 40 per cent of young graduates were jobless.He said one in six Indians aged between 15 and 29 was unemployed in July 2026 and alleged that the promise of creating two crore jobs annually had not been fulfilled.Kharge also raised concerns over rising prices, claiming retail inflation had touched a 19-month high. He said the prices of sugar, onion, tomato, pulses, cooking oil, rice and milk had increased significantly."Petrol, Diesel, LPG and CNG is becoming unaffordable. Middle class families are somehow battling to survive and the poor has given up hope," Kharge said.On inequality, Kharge alleged that wealth concentration had worsened, claiming the top 1 per cent owned 40 per cent of India's total wealth."The bottom 50% survives on a humiliating 15%. Your government has engineered the greatest transfer of wealth from the poor to the rich in independent India's history," he said to Modi.He further alleged that the Modi government had encouraged crony capitalism."Your government has written off over Rs 16 lakh crore of corporate loans since 2014. And in the latest jaw-dropping example, creditors recovered just Rs 6.5 crore against admitted claims of Rs. 22,006 crore, giving a 99.97% haircut," Kharge said.He also said Modi is functioning as a "personal travel agent for a crony friend.""Your repeated sermons of asking Indians not to buy gold and not to travel abroad shows the ground reality. Fact remains: Nothing has changed except your ability to LIE to the people!" he said in his post.Kharge's remarks came a day after Modi welcomed the country's 7.8 per cent GDP growth rate and described it as a significant achievement amid global uncertainties, geopolitical conflicts and supply chain disruptions.In a video message posted on Instagram, Modi criticised those questioning the state of the economy and said the latest growth figures had disproved narratives of pessimism surrounding India's economic prospects.Referring to what appeared to be a swipe at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's 'Chhatron ki Goonj' campaign, Modi said the GDP figures had cut through the "jhooth ki goonj" being spread about the economy.He said India must sustain its growth momentum and continue working towards greater self-reliance and promotion of 'Swadeshi'.Modi said his government's policies were sound and its intentions clear, which had helped the country achieve new milestones in development.India's economy expanded by a faster-than-expected 7.8 per cent in the April-June quarter of 2026-27, easing concerns of a slowdown triggered by the conflict in West Asia.While growth moderated from 8.6 per cent in the previous quarter, it remained above market expectations despite disruptions in global energy markets.Describing the GDP performance as a "Herculean feat", Modi on Monday said critics who had predicted a downturn had been proven wrong."doomsayers were doomed and India bloomed yet again," he said.(With Agency Inputs)
Article Summary: Mallikarjun Kharge says PM's "PR on economy" has been one of "lights, camera and inaction" He claims unemployment is at a 50-year high and that 40 per cent of young graduates are jobless. Kharge also raised concerns over rising prices, claiming retail inflation had touched a 19-month high.

Article Title: NPS charges revised from October 1, 2026: Rs 200 onboarding fee, 0.20% annual charge; e-NPS users can avoid PoP fees, check who pays and who gets relief
Article Text:
According to the PFRDA circular, PoPs will receive an annual charge equivalent to 0.20% of the assets under management.

New NPS PoP onboarding charge from October 1, 2026: What changes

One-time onboarding charge

Annual charges for all schemes under NPS and NPS Lite

Will

dormant NPS accounts

attract PoP charges?

Revised minimum contribution under NPS

Who will not have to pay PoP charges?

PoPs must display revised charges

New NPS charges from October 1: The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) has updated the charges that Point of Presence (PoP) entities are permitted to levy on subscribers under the National Pension System (NPS) and NPS Lite.These revised charges will come into effect from October 1, 2026, while Central Recordkeeping Agencies will begin implementing the deduction from the third quarter of FY 2026-27.In a circular dated August 28, 2026, PFRDA has done away with the distinction between common schemes and schemes launched under the Multiple Scheme Framework (MSF).The circular, titled ‘Standardised framework for classification and presentation of schemes under the National Pension System (NPS), also sets out the charges applicable to subscribers making contributions through e-NPS and D-Remit.Under the new fee structure, subscribers registering for NPS through a PoP will be charged a one-time onboarding fee of Rs 200 for each Permanent Retirement Account Number (PRAN).However, the entire Rs 200 will not be taken from the subscriber’s account at once.Instead, the charge will be collected at Rs 50 per quarter by cancelling units through the Central Recordkeeping Agencies (CRAs).The amount will be remitted to the PoP in the month following the quarter in which the subscriber completes the onboarding process.According to the PFRDA circular, PoPs will receive an annual charge equivalent to 0.20% of the assets under management (AUM) for all schemes, except dormant accounts. The charge will be adjusted through the net asset value (NAV) and paid to the PoP on a quarterly basis.One-time onboarding charge for digitally registered subscribersPFRDA has also specified the onboarding fee applicable to subscribers who complete their registration entirely through a digital, non-face-to-face process. In such cases, a one-time charge of Rs 100 may be levied, depending on the terms prescribed by PFRDA when the PoP is registered and any subsequent terms determined by the regulator.GST and other applicable taxes will be levied separately, according to the PFRDA circular.PFRDA has said that PoP charges will not apply to dormant accounts. It defines a dormant account as an account or accounts identified through a unique Permanent Account Number (PAN) across all CRAs where, after a contribution is made in a quarter, no further contribution is received for four consecutive quarters, as determined at the end of each quarter.The circular also lays down the minimum amounts that NPS subscribers must contribute.At the time of onboarding, a subscriber is required to contribute at least Rs 250. For subsequent contributions, the minimum contribution is Rs 10.Subscribers who opened their NPS accounts through e-NPS and subsequently make contributions through e-NPS or D-Remit will not have to pay PoP charges, according to the circular. However, those who initially onboarded through a PoP will continue to be liable for these charges even if their later contributions are made through e-NPS or D-Remit.This distinction is important because using e-NPS or D-Remit for a contribution does not, by itself, exempt a subscriber from PoP charges when the NPS account was originally opened through a PoP.PFRDA has instructed all PoPs to clearly and prominently publish their revised charge structure on their respective websites.Have charges for 4A schemes under the NPS also been revised?The new fee structure does not apply to PoP charges for 4A Schemes, including schemes launched under Regulation 4A of the Exit Regulations, such as NPS Vatsalya, NPS Swasthya and NPS MSME.PFRDA said the charges applicable to these schemes will continue to be determined by their respective guidelines and circulars.New NPS PoP charges replace earlier structureThe revised charges will supersede the PFRDA circular issued on March 10, 2026. That earlier circular prescribed PoP charges for common schemes under NPS (All Citizen), including NPS Vatsalya and NPS Lite.
Article Summary: The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) has updated the charges that Point of Presence (PoP) entities are permitted to levy on subscribers under the National Pension System (NPS) These revised charges will come into effect from October 1, 2026. PoPs will receive an annual charge equivalent to 0.20% of the assets under management.
